entities.name: PMID:10737527
observations: A cohort of 65 patients with UPJ obstruction and six normal controls used Masson's trichrome and image analysis; lower collagen-to-smooth-muscle ratio correlated with improved postoperative hydronephrosis (r=-0.50, p=0.0001) and renal function (r=-0.43, p=0.0004). Ratio ≤1 group showed better renal-function improvement than ratio >1.5 group (p=0.002).

entities.name: PMID:31500874
observations: In 31 children, one-year clinical outcome correlated strongly and inversely with collagen-to-muscle ratio measured at the ureteric anastomosis (r=-0.94, p=0.001); ratio <1.2 at that site predicted success. Retrospective/consecutive-series diagnostic-criteria study.

entities.name: PMID:15711350
observations: Among 66 evaluable patients from 75 UPJ obstruction cases, lower ratio at the UPJ was associated with greater postoperative hydronephrosis improvement, but the association was borderline (p=0.049); elastin in retained pelvis/ureter also mattered.

entities.name: PMID:31315518
observations: In 31 children, collagen-to-muscle ratio at the ureteric anastomosis correlated inversely with one-year outcome (r=-0.91, p=0.001); ratio ≤1.2 was associated with successful outcome and assessed using rapid frozen-section staining.
